Summary: Enable the MyChart mobile app in the Accordant instance
Description:
Problem Statement (Who, What, Where, When, Why):
Who: Accordant memberWhat: Enable the MyChart mobile app in the Accordant instanceWhere: Within the Accordant instance and the MyChart mobile app environment.When: During 2026 PI1.Why: To eliminate the need for a paid contract with the current vendor (Well Doc/Health Optimizer), resulting in significant cost savings, as the Epic MyChart Mobile product is included at no additional charge.

Benefit Hypothesis:
By enabling the MyChart mobile app in the Accordant instance, we will provide users with a seamless mobile experience that mirrors the web application, reduce operational costs by eliminating the vendor contract, and enhance user engagement with the healthcare services provided.

Contacts/Dependencies:
Epic Technical Support - To resolve any EPIC technical challenges during implementationEpic Client Systems - For deployment supportBusiness/Product Team - Requirement clarification

In Scope:
Replicating the current functionalities of MyChart web application's in the MyChart mobile app.Ensuring that all features available on MyChart web application's are accessible via the mobile app.Conducting functional testing to validate the mobile app's functionality.Providing training and communication to users about the transition to the MyChart mobile app. Update from Stefanie based on MyChart Mobile app demo and target plan for this feature--------------------------------Key Questions for ITBeyond 1:1 parity with our existing MyChart Web build, which items require additional configuration or development, and what is the LOE for each?What is the earliest feasible prod go-live date for the mobile app, inclusive of build, configuration, testing, UAT, and demos (e.g., uploading medications in the MyChart app and confirming the workflow back into Epic)?Are there any dependencies or constraints that could impact this timeline?Below is the organized view of MVP items, simple use cases, LOE needs, and post-MVP enhancements.Bucket 1 - Turning on MyChart (Immediate Priority)A. Expected 1:1 Web Parity (with simple use cases):• Turning on the MyChart App - Member downloads the MyChart app or connects Accordant if already installed. • Secure Messaging - Member sends a message with attachments; nurse replies in Epic.• Assessments & Questionnaires - Member completes condition-specific forms; results appear in Epic.• Education Library (Multilingual) - Member views materials in English/Spanish.• Medication Management - Member updates their medication list; nurse sees changes in Epic.• Happy Together - Member sees records from multiple health systems in one view.• Appointment Scheduling - Member schedules a call or visit with their nurse.• Multilingual Support - Full navigation in English or Spanish.• Accessibility Compliance - App is fully compatible with screen readers.• Custom Branding - Accordant and client-specific branding matches the web experience.• Device Integration (baseline) - Member connects Apple Health; vitals flow into Epic (clarification needed on what member sees across platforms).• Biometric Login - Member logs in with FaceID or fingerprint (need confirmation if this is automatically enabled)B. Items Requiring Clarification or LOE:• Push notifications enablement and default configuration - can we customize notifications and LOE• Custom deep links (e.g., linking directly from emails into the app)• Mobile vs web analytics (usage, medication logging, login counts)• AVS experience (PDF vs optimized mobile view)• Supported iOS/Android versions• Please confirm that users who have an existing MyChart account will be able to use the same username and PW to log in to the app• Is there anything we can do to help transition HO members to MyChart. Can we transition their account log-in to MyChart? Bucket 2 - Disabling Health Optimizer• Steps and sequence to sunset HO• Any dependent workflows or data flows• Required communications (banners, notifications, email outreach)• Timing relative to MyChart Mobile launchBucket 3 - MyChart Enhancements (Post-MVP)• Custom mobile app build (e.g., Penn Med model) if needed/proves to be the best member experience. Need to clarify that even if a member downloads ""custom app"" can they still access other organizations' mychart?• Simplified login experience• Improved AVS format• Expanded device integration (Bluetooth, additional wearables)• Education Video hosting------------------------------------------------------------

Any new features or enhancements beyond the current functionality of the web application's All features available in (Well Doc/Health Optimizer) are not in scope for MyChart web application

Establishing a clear framework for discovering which AI-generated notes can be accurately filed into the relevant sections of EPIC will ensure that critical clinical information from member and coach interactions is consistently captured, organized, and accessible. This will enhance care delivery by providing clinicians with timely and structured documentation, improve compliance with regulatory and organizational standards, and streamline workflows by reducing manual effort and errors. Ultimately, this approach will unlock the full potential of AI-driven documentation, supporting better patient outcomes and operational efficiency.

Description:
Participants:

Problem Statement:
A long-standing integration gap between Care Engine and Epic has resulted in inaccurate and incomplete delivery of Care Considerations (CCs) to clinical teams. Epic is not notified when CCs become historic or retracted, allowing outdated guidance to remain actionable. At the same time, valid CCs are missed due to flawed incremental and sequencing logic. Severity 1 CCs are further blocked by enrollment and responsible-user dependencies, conflicting with Policy 133 delivery requirements. Increased CC volume and visibility have elevated this from a technical defect to a clinical safety, operational, and compliance risk

Business Value:
Prevents clinicians from acting on outdated or invalid CCs, Ensures Severity 1 CCs are delivered within required timelines per Policy 133, regardless of enrollment, Reduces manual cleanup, duplicate CC generation, and workflow confusion and Ensures Epic reflects accurate, complete, and actionable CC information

Contacts/Dependencies:
Epic Integration TeamCareEngine EngineeringLCC Clinical OperationsIO Platform / Integration ServicesCM (Care Management) Product & OpsScope: 1. Look back time to send the Hist/Retracted CC's- 3 or 6 or 12 months?Example:CC's got generated on 3/1/2026LCC Identified on 4/1/2026 then send all the Active CC's on 4/1/2026if any CC's got Historic/retracted on or after 4/1/2026 then sent only those to EPIC 3. Close the Feedback LoopEpic must send CC disposition back to CareEngine that a CC was communicated/delivered in EPICDisposition codes to be reviewed to make sure all the disposition codes are mapped in ODS or notThis prevents duplicate CC generation and infinite loops 4. Prevent Delivery of Invalid CCs in EPIC by Clinical OperationsWhen a CC becomes historic or retracted, Epic must automatically cancel or remove the associated taskVisibility of historic/retracted status to end users can see it in EPICAgreed direction:Remove the task/CC in EPIC when CC becomes HIST or Retracted 5. Deliver Severity 1 CCs Regardless of EnrollmentSeverity 1 CCs must trigger task creation even if the member is not enrolled in LCCDuplicate task creation must be preventedEnrollment status must not block deliveryAgreed direction:All Sev 1 CCs must trigger task creation, regardless of LCC enrollment or responsible user.If no coach exists, task should be routed to a pool/bucket for supervisor assignment. 6. Summary: Health Advisor report - migrating Teradata table to BigQuery Phase 2
Description:
Problem Statement (Who, What, Where, When, Why):
CSS and RetroDUR are planned for retirement in Q2 2026. Their replacement application, Clinical Rx Manager (CRxM), is scheduled to go live in mid to late Q2 2026.Once CRxM becomes the active system, it will begin sending all data to Google Cloud Platform (GCP) instead of the legacy data sources. To ensure uninterrupted downstream consumption, analytics, and reporting, the current EDW processes must transition from sourcing data in the legacy CSS/RetroDUR environments to sourcing data directly from GCP-hosted CRxM datasets.This feature ensures that data pipelines, transformations, and datasets dependent on CSS/RetroDUR structures are updated to reflect the new CRxM data model, including any changes to table names, data types, and relationships.

Benefit Hypothesis:
Implementing this feature will:Ensure continuity of EDW processing after CSS and RetroDUR retirement.Align data sourcing with the CRxM architecture and prevent data gaps.Support long-term maintainability by adopting modern GCP data structures.Mitigate business risk by proactively updating pipelines ahead of legacy decommissioning.Expected areas of change include:Table Name Changes - CRxM datasets will differ from existing EDW table structures.Data Type Changes - Source system transformations may require schema updates.Relationship Changes - Join logic may change due to revised CRxM data modeling.

Contacts/Dependencies:
CRxM Product Team - Source system owners, data model documentationGCP Data Engineering - Pipeline availability, dataset accessCSS / RetroDUR Retirement Program - Timeline for sunset activitiesEDW Architecture - Approvals and data lineage validationDownstream Consumer Teams - Validation and UAT of updated datasets

In Scope:
The following legacy EDW views and relationships must be evaluated and transitioned to GCP-sourced CRxM equivalents:DWU_EDW_RB.V_CSS_CLNT_PGM_DLY_HIST as d DWU_EDW_RB.V_CSS_CLNT_PGM_CPG_HIST as g on d.clnt_pgm_id = g.clnt_pgm_id -- get lvl3_acct_gid for the associated cpg_id; cpg_id is not PK; cpg_id can be mapped to multiple lvl3_acct_id DWU_EDW_RB.V_QL_CLNT_ACCT_HRCHY as h on g.CPG_ID = h.CPG_ID DWU_EDW_RB.V_CLNT_ACCT_DENORM as clnt on h.LVL3_ACCT_GID = clnt.LVL3_ACCT_GID DWU_EDW_RB.V_CSS_CLNT_PGM_CMPNT_HIST as p on d.clnt_pgm_id = p.clnt_pgm_idDWU_EDW_RB.V_CSS_PGM_CMPNT_HIST as c on p.clnt_pgm_cmpnt_cd = c.pgm_cmpnt_cd

Out of Scope:

Assumptions:
These assumptions outline what must be true for this feature to succeed:CRxM will deliver complete and validated data models to EDW before integration work begins.All required CRxM datasets will be available and accessible in GCP within the expected timeline.EDW will receive accurate mapping documentation from CRxM to reconcile differences with legacy CSS/RetroDUR schemas.No additional legacy data backfill is required beyond what CRxM provides.Data governance, security roles, and GCP access will be in place prior to development.Downstream consumers will participate in UAT for validation and certification of new GCP-sourced datasets.Existing business logic remains valid unless CRxM explicitly defines a new rule or structure.

Outstanding Questions:

Success Criteria:
& Metrics:This feature is considered successful when:All CSS and RetroDUR dependencies for the listed EDW tables are fully replaced with CRxM/GCP equivalents.EDW pipelines process CRxM data successfully and without interruption.All schema changes (tables, datatypes, relationships) are updated and validated.Downstream reports and dashboards continue to function correctly with CRxM-sourced data.Data quality checks meet established thresholds with no material gaps.Historical and current data align with expected business definitions.All business stakeholders sign off that the new pipelines can replace legacy sourcing before CSS/RetroDUR retirement.The system is ready before the CRxM go-live window (mid-late Q2 2026). ----
